title: Coloring and fusing architectural sketches by combining a Y‐shaped generative adversarial network and a denoising diffusion implicit model

methodology_steps.description: Data Collection and Augmentation: The researchers collected a base set of architectural photos and expanded them into a larger dataset using common augmentation methods such as scaling, cutting, and mirror transition to ensure model robustness
data_inputs:
600 initial photos of low-rise buildings collected from the internet
Software Tools/Libraries: Version not stated
expected_outputs: An augmented architectural dataset consisting of 10,000 images

methodology_steps.description:
Input Pre-processing and Standardization: Each color image is converted into a corresponding sketch using the XDoG operator to create a paired training set
. Additionally, all sketches and color images are resized to a uniform resolution of 256 × 256 pixels
data_inputs:
RGB architectural images from the augmented dataset
Software Tools/Libraries: extended difference-of-Gaussians (XDoG) operator
expected_outputs: A standardized dataset of paired 256 × 256 pixel sketches and RGB images

methodology_steps.description:
Neural Network Training: The Y-shaped GAN is trained for one day to minimize reconstruction, adversarial, and perceptual losses
. The U-Net-based DDIM is trained for five days on colorful architectural data to learn the distribution of realistic building structures
data_inputs:
Standardized pairs of sketches and color images (for GAN training) and colorful architectural data (for DDIM training)
Software Tools/Libraries: Adam solver for optimization
VGG-19 model pretrained on ImageNet for perceptual losses

versions not stated
. Training was performed on one 12-GB NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070Ti GPU
expected_outputs: A trained Y-shaped GAN generator and a trained DDIM noise estimator

methodology_steps.description:
Reference-Based Sketch Coloring (Phase I): The input sketch is standardized via XDoG
. The GAN uses a two-headed encoder to separate the sketch's spatial information from the reference's color information
. The AM module matches these domains, while a bifurcated flow (via skip connections) sends sketch features directly to the decoder to ensure the output respects the original building layout
data_inputs:
A target architectural sketch (Is) and a temporarily specified reference image (Ir)
Software Tools/Libraries: Y-shaped GAN (proposed by the authors) utilizing an Attention Mechanism (AM) module and ResNet layers
expected_outputs: A color rendering that correctly matches the spatial layout of the sketch with the color palette, textures, and atmospheric "mood" of the reference image

methodology_steps.description: Design Fusion — Intermediate Coloring: Both target sketches are first colored using the same reference image via the Y-shaped GAN to ensure they share a common color distribution
data_inputs:
Two different architectural sketches and a shared reference image
Software Tools/Libraries: Y-shaped GAN
expected_outputs: A pair of color-similar intermediate images

methodology_steps.description:
Linear Interpolation (The "Interpolation Trick"): Instead of interpolating latent vectors after encoding, the researchers perform linear interpolation on the image pixels themselves before encoding
. This "trick" is necessary to avoid generating "meaningless intermediate states" during the fusion process
data_inputs:
The pair of color-similar intermediate images
Software Tools/Libraries: Version not stated
expected_outputs: An interim "fuzzy" image (It=0) representing the blended state of the two designs

methodology_steps.description:
Deterministic Encoding via DDIM: The fuzzy image is encoded into latent vectors (It=T) using a deterministic iterative process where the random factor (σ
t
	​

) is eliminated to ensure stable mapping
data_inputs:
The interim fuzzy image
Software Tools/Libraries: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model (DDIM)
expected_outputs: Latent vectors that represent the fused architectural state

methodology_steps.description: Structural Refinement and Sampling: The latent vectors are decoded through the DDIM reverse process. During this stage, the DDIM acts as a deblurring network, using a random factor (σ) of approximately 0.1 to remove blurs and restore structural logic
data_inputs:
Latent vectors from the encoding step
Software Tools/Libraries: DDIM reverse sampling process
expected_outputs: A final harmonious architectural design that preserves linear, rectangular, and gravity-based characteristics of buildings

datasets.description: A collection of architectural images representing low-rise buildings used for training and evaluation [2].
Corresponding sketch images created using the extended difference-of-Gaussians (XDoG) operator [2, 5].
A large-scale image database used for pre-training the VGG-19 model [6].
A dataset containing multiple categories of objects used for diverse sketch-to-image synthesis [7].
Labeled images of apartment floor plans used for recognizing and generating architectural drawings [9, 10].
Datasets used in prior multiheaded GAN research, such as Lee's GAN and SC-FEGAN, for reference-based coloring [11, 12].

hardware_requirements:
one 12-GB NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070Ti GPU
Hyperparameters: lambda_r: 20 (Weight for reconstruction loss in the Y-shaped GAN objective function); lambda_a: 1 (Weight for adversarial loss in the Y-shaped GAN objective function); lambda_f: 0.01 (Weight for feature reconstruction loss in the Y-shaped GAN objective function); lambda_s: 1 (Weight for style reconstruction loss in the Y-shaped GAN objective function); learning rate: 0.0002 (Constant rate applied to both the generator and discriminator using the Adam solver); batch size: 1 (Setting used for all training processes in the study); T (diffusion steps): 1000 (Default number of steps for training the denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM)); sigma (random factor): 0.1 (Preferable setting used during the DDIM reverse sampling process to remove blurs and restore architectural logic; utilized within a tested range of 0 to 0.2); m (interpolation factor): 0 to 1 (Range used to balance the fusion of two disparate architectural designs)
